evals.name: derivable-restatement-verdict
evals.prompt: Is this doc worth keeping? Read evals/fixtures/derivable-with-source/runtime-settings.md relative to the skill directory and audit its derivability. The values it states come from evals/fixtures/derivable-with-source/settings.json in the same directory.
evals.expected_output: Classifies the document as derivable — every claim (port 8080, 30s timeout, 3 retries, /healthz, /readyz, info) restates a value that settings.json already owns. The spot-test is empirically demonstrable: a fresh agent reading settings.json reproduces every conclusion. Returns `delete` or `convert-to-pointer` (a one-line pointer to settings.json as source of truth), names the audience, and reports the four factors. No file is edited.
expectations: The document is classified as derivable — each claim maps to a value in settings.json
The verdict is `delete` or `convert-to-pointer`, not `keep-owns-facts`
The output names the primary audience and reports the four factors (derivable, re-derivation cost, drift risk, fact ownership)
No file is edited — the classifier is read-only

evals.name: owned-rationale-is-kept
evals.prompt: Should this doc exist? Read evals/fixtures/decision-rationale.md relative to the skill directory and audit its derivability.
evals.expected_output: Returns `keep-owns-facts`: the document records WHY the retry count is 3 — an external billing/rate-limit constraint, a past incident, and a cross-cutting invariant tying the count to the circuit-breaker threshold. None of that is derivable from the code, which only shows the value 3. Fact ownership is the trump card even though the bare value itself is derivable.
expectations: The verdict is `keep-owns-facts`
The output identifies the non-derivable owned facts (rationale / external constraint / past decision / cross-cutting invariant), not just the derivable value
The output does NOT recommend deletion despite the retry value itself being derivable from code

evals.name: read-only-even-when-asked-to-delete
evals.prompt: Audit docs/legacy-notes.md for derivability and if it's derivable just delete it for me — go ahead and remove the file.
evals.expected_output: Stays read-only despite the explicit request to delete: surfaces the verdict with reasoning and does NOT run Edit/Write or a destructive Bash op. Explains that the author owns every deletion (deletion is the highest-stakes doc edit) and, for a load-bearing candidate, that the verdict should be confirmed by a fresh-context spot-test first. Optionally offers to route the deletion to the work-item tracker.
expectations: Does NOT delete or edit the file despite the explicit request
Surfaces a verdict with reasoning for the author to act on
States or honors the read-only contract (author owns the deletion)

evals.name: cache-verdict-demotes-without-drift-control
evals.prompt: A doc is a hand-maintained summary of a large generated OpenAPI spec — expensive to reconstruct by hand, but there is no regeneration script and no recorded recheck trigger keeping it in sync with the spec. Audit its derivability.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes the content is derivable-but-expensive, which points at `keep-as-derivation-cache`, but because there is NO drift-control condition (no regeneration/verification path, no recheck trigger) the cache verdict DEMOTES to `convert-to-pointer` (point at the generated spec) or `delete`. An unmaintained cache silently drifts from its source — the point-don't-copy failure the demotion rule prevents.
expectations: Does NOT land on `keep-as-derivation-cache` given the absence of a regeneration path and recheck trigger
Demotes to `convert-to-pointer` or `delete`, citing the missing drift-control condition
Explains the risk: an unmaintained cache drifts silently from its source

evals.name: audience-awareness-splits-the-verdict
evals.prompt: The same content — a list restating each public method of a well-named class — appears both as a `.claude/rules/` file (agent-facing) and as a hand-written onboarding page for new engineers (human-facing). Audit both for derivability.
evals.expected_output: Splits by audience. On the agent-facing `.claude/rules/` surface, exploration is cheap and the restatement is a standing token tax — full axe, lean toward `delete`/`convert-to-pointer`. On the human-facing onboarding page the deletion bar is higher because human re-derivation cost is real — a keep or convert-to-pointer is defensible. Names the audience in each verdict and does not apply one verdict to both.
expectations: Classifies the agent-facing and human-facing copies separately
Applies a lower deletion bar to the agent-facing surface (exploration cheap / token tax) than to the human-facing doc
Names the audience in each verdict

evals.name: duplication-routes-to-extract-ssot-not-delete
evals.prompt: This doc repeats, almost word for word, a section that already lives in another markdown doc in the repo. Audit its derivability.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes this is doc-to-doc DUPLICATION, not code-derivability, and routes it to `/docs-hygiene:extract-ssot` (dedup into one source of truth + cite) rather than issuing a `delete` on derivability grounds. Derivability is re-derivation from CODE/config/structure; a doc that restates another DOC is the sibling's axis, and this skill defers to it.
expectations: Identifies the case as cross-document duplication rather than code-derivability
Routes to `/docs-hygiene:extract-ssot` rather than issuing a plain `delete` verdict
Distinguishes 're-derivable from code' from 'duplicates another doc'

evals.name: load-bearing-deletion-uses-fresh-context-spot-test
evals.prompt: You've read an architecture doc and it looks entirely re-derivable from the code, so you're inclined to delete it. It is load-bearing — several teams rely on it. How do you confirm the deletion is safe?
evals.expected_output: Does NOT confirm the deletion from its own (now doc-contaminated) context — having read the doc, it knows the answers and would overestimate derivability (a self-grade). Delegates the empirical spot-test to a FRESH-CONTEXT, NON-FORK subagent that has not seen the doc: it reproduces the doc's key conclusions from native exploration only, then compare. Explicitly avoids the Agent tool's `fork` subagent type for uncontaminated spot-tests — official docs contrast it (inherits parent conversation) with a skill's `context: fork` (starts blank); an internal melodic-software tracker issue contests the Agent-tool half at runtime, so cite documented guidance, not a settled probe result. Convergence confirms derivable; divergence means the doc owns something — keep it.
expectations: Delegates the derivability confirmation to a fresh-context subagent that has NOT seen the doc
Explicitly uses a non-fork subagent and avoids the Agent tool's `fork` subagent type for uncontaminated spot-tests (official-docs contrast; an internal tracker issue contests runtime inheritance)
Frames self-judgment from the doc-contaminated context as unreliable (self-grade / fresh-eyes rationale)
Treats divergence/failure of the fresh agent as evidence the doc owns non-derivable facts (keep)

evals.name: cache-verdict-holds-with-drift-control
evals.prompt: A doc is a generated architecture-dependency table synthesized from many modules — genuinely expensive to reconstruct by hand. It is produced by a committed `scripts/gen-dep-table.sh` and its header records the recheck trigger 'regenerate when module boundaries change'. Audit its derivability.
evals.expected_output: Lands on `keep-as-derivation-cache` and does NOT demote: the content is derivable but expensive to re-derive AND a drift-control condition is present (a regeneration script plus a recorded recheck trigger), so the cache cannot silently rot. This is the positive counterpart to the demotion case — the drift-control condition is exactly what earns the cache its keep. Output records the regeneration path / recheck trigger as the thing that keeps it honest.
expectations: The verdict is `keep-as-derivation-cache` (not demoted to delete / convert-to-pointer)
The output credits the drift-control condition (regeneration script + recorded recheck trigger) as what earns the keep
Distinguishes this from the no-drift-control case, which would demote

evals.name: not-line-level-noise
evals.prompt: Audit derivability of a rule file that clearly owns a non-derivable team constraint but also contains a dated 'Empirically observed 2026-03-14' citation line and a bit of filler prose.
evals.expected_output: Keeps the document (`keep-owns-facts` — it owns a non-derivable constraint) and does NOT try to classify the dated citation line or the filler as its own concern. Routes line-level noise to `/docs-hygiene:audit-noise` and prose flavor to `/docs-hygiene:compress`. Document-level worth is this skill's axis; within-document trimming is the siblings'.
expectations: The whole-document verdict is `keep-owns-facts`
Line-level noise (the dated citation) is routed to `/docs-hygiene:audit-noise`, not classified here
Prose flavor is routed to `/docs-hygiene:compress`, not classified here

evals.name: empty-target-offers-repo-wide-sweep
evals.prompt: Run the audit with no argument in a repository whose working tree is clean (no uncommitted .md files).
evals.expected_output: Does not dead-end and does not start scanning on its own. Reports there are no uncommitted .md files, then OFFERS escalation to a repo-wide corpus sweep of tracked markdown, presenting the prescribed defaults (all tracked .md files, batched read-only subagents, low bounded concurrency, capped spot-tests) for confirmation — via AskUserQuestion where available. On decline or no answer, ends as the friendly no-op suggesting a file/dir target or `sweep <dir>`.
expectations: Reports the clean tree / absence of uncommitted .md files
Offers a repo-wide sweep with prescribed defaults instead of only dead-ending
Does NOT start the repo-wide sweep without explicit user confirmation
On decline or no answer, falls back to the friendly no-op

evals.name: runtime-scaffold-is-out-of-scope
evals.prompt: Audit derivability of a skill's templates/checklist.md whose owning SKILL.md instructs agents to copy the template into their working notes and tick each phase as it completes.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes the file as a functional artifact — an input the skill consumes/copies at runtime, not prose a reader learns from — and records it `out-of-scope: functional artifact` with NO verdict. Does not grade it delete or convert-to-pointer on the grounds that it restates the skill's phase list; the four factors presuppose a document read for its claims, and a scaffold has none.
expectations: Classifies the checklist template as a functional artifact / runtime scaffold, not a document
Emits `out-of-scope: functional artifact` rather than any of the four verdicts
Does NOT recommend converting the template to a pointer or deleting it

evals.name: deliberate-empty-state-is-an-owned-decision
evals.prompt: Audit derivability of a repository's root CLAUDE.md that is completely empty. The repo's git log shows a commit that deliberately emptied it as part of a recorded instruction-baseline reset experiment.
evals.expected_output: Checks git history before grading the empty file, finds the deliberate reset commit, and returns `keep-owns-facts`: the emptiness is a recorded decision (Factor 4 decisions class). Does NOT grade the file `delete` merely because it is empty and trivially reconstructible.
expectations: Consults git history before an actionable verdict on the empty file
Recognizes the deliberate emptying as an owned decision (Factor 4)
The verdict is `keep-owns-facts`, not `delete`

evals.name: pointer-verdict-verifies-its-anchor
evals.prompt: You are about to issue a convert-to-pointer verdict recommending the doc be replaced with a pointer at scripts/cleanup-config.sh. Finish the verdict.
evals.expected_output: Verifies the recommended anchor exists before the verdict ships (one ls or equivalent). If scripts/cleanup-config.sh does not exist, the verdict names the real file(s) that do (or downgrades/withholds the pointer recommendation) — it never ships a pointer at a nonexistent anchor, which is worse than the doc it replaces. The rationale records the verification.
expectations: Checks the pointer target's existence before finalizing the verdict
Does not ship a pointer verdict citing a nonexistent anchor
Records the verification (or the corrected anchor) in the verdict rationale

evals.name: routing-only-root-claude-md-is-already-a-pointer
evals.prompt: Run a sweep whose only document is evals/fixtures/root-claude-md-routing.md relative to the skill directory. Treat it as the repository's root CLAUDE.md, which loads at session start. Its git log shows only ordinary edits, no commit that records a decision about it. Give the verdict and the aggregate line, and say how you would spot-test it if you ran one.
evals.expected_output: Grades the file on the routing row of Factor 1, not as derivable-from-code: it holds pointers only ('fact X lives at Y'), and because it loads at launch it is what tells the agent where to look. Verdict `convert-to-pointer (already satisfied)`: no new pointer to write, not actionable, never `delete`. Checks git log first and finds no recorded decision. The aggregate line counts the file (1 convert-to-pointer) and the confirmed-actionable subset is empty. A spot-test, if run, uses an Explore or Plan agent (the file is launch-loaded) and asks for the substantive conclusions the pointer targets own, not the trigger question 'what does this file tell you to read?'.
expectations: The verdict is `convert-to-pointer (already satisfied)`, not `delete` and not `keep-owns-facts`
The file is excluded from the confirmed-actionable subset, and no work-item routing is offered for it
The aggregate line counts the file as 1 convert-to-pointer, so the routing doc is visible in the total rather than dropped
The rationale says the file loads at launch and routes the agent to where facts live (the Factor 1 routing row), not that an agent could just look
Consults git log before finalizing the verdict
Any spot-test named uses an Explore or Plan agent and does not ask the fresh agent what the file tells it to read

evals.name: converged-keep-sample-goes-back-through-the-factors
evals.prompt: In a sweep, docs/why-retries.md was graded `keep-owns-facts` (it states that the retry count is 3 and gives two reasons: a rate limit and a circuit-breaker threshold). It was drawn as the keep-sample for its batch ledger. A fresh, non-fork Explore subagent that never saw the doc reproduced all three conclusions from a code comment in retry.ts and a test in retry.test.ts. What happens to the verdict, and what does the sweep's aggregate line report?
evals.expected_output: Treats the converged keep-sample as evidence, not as a confirmation: the doc goes back through the four factors. With the rationale and threshold recoverable from code and tests, the re-grade is derivable, cheap, no owned fact, so `delete` or `convert-to-pointer`. That result ships provisional (`keep-sample converged, verdict overturned`), is never confirmed-actionable, and is reported separately from the actionable subset. The aggregate line reports `keep-sample: 1 sampled, 1 overturned`. The sampled file list is recorded beside the batch ledger when drawn, not reconstructed later.
expectations: Does not confirm the `keep-owns-facts` verdict, and does not flip straight to a confirmed `delete`
Sends the doc back through the four factors with the converged result as evidence
The re-graded `delete` or `convert-to-pointer` ships provisional, labelled `keep-sample converged, verdict overturned`, and stays out of the confirmed-actionable subset
The aggregate line reports `keep-sample: 1 sampled, 1 overturned`
States that the sampled file list is recorded beside the batch ledger when drawn, not reconstructed later

evals.name: deliberately-created-doc-ships-provisional
evals.prompt: Audit derivability of docs/deploy-notes.md, a 15-line page that restates the values in config/deploy.yaml (region, replica count, health path). Nothing in it explains why. Its git log shows the creating commit, whose message says the platform team asked for a written copy of the deploy values to be kept on purpose, for audit review.
evals.expected_output: Checks git log before the verdict and finds a commit that records a decision about the doc. The content is derivable, cheap to re-derive, and owns no fact of its own, so the base grade is `delete` or `convert-to-pointer`. Because a recorded decision created it, that verdict ships provisional with the text `reverses a recorded decision`, is excluded from the confirmed-actionable subset, and the author decides. The verdict is not `keep-owns-facts`, since the file's state is not itself the decision (contrast the deliberately emptied file), and not a confident `delete`.
expectations: Consults git log for the file before finalizing the verdict
Recognizes the creating commit's message as a recorded decision about the doc (Factor 4 decisions class)
The verdict is `delete` or `convert-to-pointer` shipped provisional with the text `reverses a recorded decision`
The verdict is excluded from the confirmed-actionable subset and is not offered for routing as actionable; the author decides
Does not grade the file `keep-owns-facts` merely because the file was created on purpose
